lecture_summary: Torque geometry and direction—moment arms, force angle, and the right-hand rule—followed by fixed-axis rotational dynamics using extended free-body diagrams, Στ = Iα, and additive moments of inertia. Examples include a door, an angled wrench, a cord-driven spool, and rigidly attached cylinders.

videos.title: Torque, Basic Introduction, Lever Arm, Moment of Force, Simple Machines & Mechanical Advantage
videos.reason: Establishes torque, lever arms, pivot distance, and rotational signs through leverage examples analogous to the lecture’s door and wrench problems.

videos.title: Inertia - Basic Introduction, Torque, Angular Acceleration, Newton's Second Law, Rotational Motion
videos.reason: Connects torque with angular acceleration through rotational Newton’s second law and explains how mass distribution determines moments of inertia, including disks.

videos.title: Rotational Dynamics - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Adds applied practice with tension and rotating pulleys, providing the closest playlist analogue to the spool problem and its free-body-diagram/torque-equation workflow.

coverage_gaps: No strong mechanics match explicitly covers the cross-product right-hand rule and into/out-of-page torque notation.
The exact wrench strategy of finding the included angle from complementary geometry, plus line-of-action geometry d = r sin θ, is not confirmed by the playlist descriptions.
No strong exact match covers a fixed-spindle spool where a nonzero pivot force has zero torque, or rigidly attached coaxial cylinders whose moments of inertia are added to solve for an unknown mass.
Symbolic-first algebra and explicit dimensional checks are not specifically represented.
